# CodeFlow ### The codebase map that proves its answers. CodeFlow maps how a JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, C# or C/C++ codebase fits together, answers questions cited to real files and lines, and **checks the code references in anyone's answer** — an AI agent's, a PR description's, a reviewer's — against the repository. The graph is scored against each language's own toolchain (the TypeScript compiler, `go list`, javac, Roslyn, clang, Python's import system); the checker runs offline, with no key. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-strict-3178c6.svg) ![Runs with Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/run%20with-Docker%20Compose-2496ed.svg)
--- ## Map · Check · Ask | | What it gives you | Commands | Measured | |---|---|---|---| | **Map** | The resolved dependency and call graph of a repository: load-bearing files, cycles, communities, blast radius, entry points, files nothing uses | `analyze`, `unused` | Import graph vs each language's own toolchain on 29 repositories (TS/JS, Go, Java, C#, C/C++, Python): precision 100% on 22, ≥ 98.4% on the other 7 (every difference explained); recall ≥ 99.5% — [tables](#measured-not-asserted-the-import-graph-vs-each-languages-own-toolchain) | | **Check** | In CI, offline: what a change touches, which tests to run, architecture rules, wrong code references in a PR description — and a PR comment only when something needs a human | `impact`, `tests`, `check`, `verify`, the GitHub Action | Test selection by fault injection: 0 of 193 failures missed while skipping 80% of a suite — [details](#check-an-answer-or-a-pr) | | **Ask** | Give an agent (Claude Code, Cursor) the graph over MCP, so it asks instead of searching file by file | the MCP server | On "what is affected" questions: half the turns, 40–46% lower cost, same accuracy — [benchmark](#claude-code-alone-vs-claude-code--codeflow) | ```bash # From a checkout (pnpm install && pnpm --filter "codeflow-local..." build); `npx codeflow-local` once published. CF="node apps/local-cli/dist/index.js" $CF analyze /path/to/repo # the map, offline, in seconds (Kubernetes: 21 s) $CF impact /path/to/repo --base main # what this branch touches $CF tests /path/to/repo --base main | xargs npx vitest run # run only the tests it can affect $CF check /path/to/repo # architecture rules from codeflow.rules.json ``` Ask, from Claude Code: analyse once, then register the server (graph and verifier tools, no key): ```bash $CF analyze /path/to/repo --no-index --out /path/to/repo/.codeflow/result.json claude mcp add codeflow -e CODEFLOW_MCP_RESULT=/path/to/repo/.codeflow/result.json \ -e CODEFLOW_MCP_SCOPES=graph,verify -- node /path/to/Code_Flow/apps/mcp/dist/index.js ``` --- ## The hosted pipeline Give CodeFlow a repository URL and it runs an **8-stage pipeline** — streamed to the browser as it happens — that turns source into a map you can interrogate. | # | Stage | What it produces | Needs a key? | |---|-------|------------------|---| | 1 | **Ingest** | shallow-clones the repo, resolves the commit SHA | no | | 2 | **Orient** | manifests, languages, frameworks, README | no | | 3 | **Map structure** | the full file tree, classified by role | no | | 4 | **Inventory** | symbols (functions/classes/…) + entry points | no | | 5 | **Connect** | the import graph, plus call/inheritance edges | no | | 6 | **Analyze** | centrality, fan-in/out, blast radius, cycles, communities | no | | 7 | **Synthesize** | a grounded onboarding summary + ranked reading order | **yes** (chat) | | 8 | **Index for Q&A** | a hybrid retrieval index so you can ask questions | **yes** (embeddings) | Stages 1–6 are deterministic and always run. 7 and 8 register only when the matching provider key is configured; without one the run completes as `deterministic-only` and **says so** rather than sitting at "pending" forever. ### The one claim worth checking **An answer cannot cite a file or line that was not actually read.** That is enforced structurally, not by prompting: the model is only permitted to emit a *chunk id*, and the file path and line range are read off the chunk that was genuinely retrieved. A fabricated line number is not rejected — it cannot be expressed. Layered on top: reading-order steps whose file is not a real graph node are dropped and counted, an entirely ungrounded synthesis is rejected outright, and `answered: true` with no surviving evidence is downgraded to a refusal. Citation chips link to GitHub **at the analysed commit**, so you can follow any claim to the source it came from. The same check is available for text CodeFlow did **not** write: `codeflow-local verify`, the `verify_citations` MCP tool and the GitHub Action take any prose and mark every `path:line`, GitHub link and named symbol as verified, unverifiable or wrong. See [Check an answer or a PR](#check-an-answer-or-a-pr). ### Measured, not asserted: the import graph vs each language's own toolchain **TypeScript / JavaScript**, against the TypeScript compiler. `scripts/graph-accuracy.mjs` resolves every import in a repository with `ts.resolveModuleName` under the nearest `tsconfig` — what `tsc` itself does — and compares each one with CodeFlow's edge for the same `(file, specifier)`. Measured on 2026-11-16 at each repository's default-branch HEAD: | Repository | In-repo imports (per tsc) | Agree | Wrong | Missed | Precision | Recall | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | trpc/trpc (pnpm monorepo) | 2,753 | 2,751 | 0 | 2 | 100% | 99.93% | | colinhacks/zod (NodeNext `.js`→`.ts`) | 823 | 821 | 0 | 2 | 100% | 99.76% | | CodeFlow itself | 824 | 824 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | shadcn-ui/taxonomy (`@/` aliases) | 260 | 260 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | expressjs/express | 154 | 154 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | The four misses are imports written inside `declare module "…" { … }` blocks. CodeFlow additionally maps workspace-package imports (`@acme/ui`) to their **source** files, which tsc can only resolve to a built `dist/`; those are reported as "extra" by the script rather than counted either way. CI runs the same check on this repository and fails below 100% precision / 99% recall. **Go**, against the Go toolchain. `scripts/accuracy/go.mjs` asks `go list -deps -test` — in every module, with each repository's own `replace`, `go.work` and vendoring — which directory every import resolves to, and compares it with CodeFlow's edge. CodeFlow points a Go import at the file that declares what is used (`store.Open` → the file declaring `Open`), so an edge agrees when its target is in the directory `go list` chose. Measured on 2026-11-16: | Repository | Layout | In-repo imports (per `go list`) | Wrong | Missed | Precision | Recall | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | kubernetes/kubernetes | 40 modules, staging + `replace` | 59,823 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | gohugoio/hugo | 4 modules | 2,222 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | etcd-io/etcd | 14 modules, `go.work` | 2,124 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | etcd-io/etcd v3.3.27 | GOPATH era, no `go.mod` | 1,262 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | spf13/cobra | 1 module | 7 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | For the GOPATH-era repository the import prefix it was checked out under is inferred from its own imports (`github.com/coreos/etcd`); `go list` ran in GOPATH mode at that path. "Extra" edges — CodeFlow has one, `go list` does not — are all files behind build tags (`_windows.go`, `//go:build tools`), which a default `go list` skips. CI runs the etcd check and fails below 100% precision / 99% recall. Kubernetes (26,558 files) analyses in 20.7 s on a laptop. **Java**, against javac. `scripts/accuracy/JavaTruth.java` runs javac's own attribution (the Compiler Tree API) over every source file and records each name that resolves to a type declared in the repository — imports, same-package types (Java needs no import for those), nested and fully qualified names. CodeFlow's file-to-file edges are compared with that set. Measured on 2026-11-16: | Repository | Layout | Edges (per javac) | CodeFlow-only | Missed | Precision | Recall | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | apache/ant | legacy Ant layout (`src/main/org/…`) | 5,725 | 7 | 3 | 99.88% | 99.95% | | junit-team/junit4 | Maven, Java 5 era | 2,474 | 0 | 3 | 100% | 99.88% | | apache/commons-lang | Maven | 1,783 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | jhy/jsoup | Maven | 1,425 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | google/gson | Maven, multi-module | 1,326 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | Every remaining difference is the reference, not CodeFlow: the truth compiles without third-party jars, so where a file explicitly imports a library class (`javax.mail.Message`, hamcrest's `TypeSafeMatcher`) javac falls back to a same-named class in the file's own package; and Ant's test fixtures declare the same class in several directories, which one javac run maps to the first copy. CI runs the jsoup check and fails below 100% precision / 99% recall. **C#**, against Roslyn (the C# compiler). `scripts/accuracy/csharp-truth/` compiles every `.csproj` the way MSBuild hands it to the compiler — its Compile items, its project references, its global usings, and the preprocessor symbols of every target framework in Debug and Release — and records each name the compiler binds to a type declared in the repository. It uses the Roslyn shipped inside the .NET SDK; nothing is downloaded from NuGet. CodeFlow reads the same `.csproj` files (references, `` items, which files an old-style project compiles) but never runs MSBuild or the compiler. Measured on 2026-11-16: | Repository | Layout | Edges (per Roslyn) | CodeFlow-only | Missed | Precision | Recall | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | App-vNext/Polly | 21 projects, multi-target | 6,849 | 6 | 0 | 99.91% | 100% | | JamesNK/Newtonsoft.Json | 8 target frameworks, .NET 2.0 → .NET 10 | 5,564 | 49 | 0 | 99.13% | 100% | | nunit/nunitv2 | legacy: 59 old-style (2005-era) projects | 4,435 | 3 | 0 | 99.93% | 100% | | serilog/serilog | SDK-style | 955 | 1 | 0 | 99.90% | 100% | | jbogard/MediatR | SDK-style, 15 projects | 531 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | CodeFlow reads both sides of every `#if`; the compiler reads only the side a project builds. That is most of the CodeFlow-only edges: Newtonsoft.Json's polyfills (`LinqBridge`, `TraceLevel`, `SerializationBinder`, …) exist for frameworks none of its projects builds today, Polly has a Windows-only test target, and Serilog a `TimeProvider` for pre-.NET 8 builds. The rest: two "Color Color" member accesses (a property named like its type, used as `TestName.Name`), an internal class Polly shows its tests through its own MSBuild item (which the reference build cannot read), WinForms code a Linux build cannot bind, and one NUnit name the reference build does not bind (not traced further). CI runs the MediatR check and fails below 100% precision / 99% recall. **C/C++**, against clang. `scripts/accuracy/c.mjs` has CMake write `compile_commands.json` — every file's real `-I`/`-D` flags — then compiles each translation unit with clang 21, which reports every file it opened and what each of its `#include`s resolved to (include-guarded re-includes too). CodeFlow never sees the build flags; it follows the compiler's search order from the repository alone. Measured on 2026-11-16: | Repository | Language | In-repo includes (per clang) | Wrong | Missed | Precision | Recall | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | libuv/libuv | C | 510 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | google/leveldb | C++ | 310 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | fmtlib/fmt | C++ | 125 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | madler/zlib | C, legacy | 39 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | Includes in `#if` branches a Linux build does not take (`uv/win.h`, `uv/os390.h`) are real edges the compiler never opens, so they are reported but not judged. CI runs the libuv check. **Python**, against Python's own import machinery. `scripts/accuracy/python-truth.py` reads each file's imports with `ast` (nothing is executed) and locates every name with `importlib.machinery.PathFinder`, the finder `import` uses, segment by segment — from `src/`, the repository root, every nested project, and the first non-package directory above the file (what pytest and `python -m` put on the path). Measured on 2026-11-16: | Repository | In-repo imports (per Python) | CodeFlow-only | Missed | Precision | Recall | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | django/django | 9,192 | 3 | 0 | 99.97% | 100% | | pallets/flask | 190 | 3 | 0 | 98.45% | 100% | | pallets/click | 171 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | encode/httpx | 122 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | | psf/requests | 108 | 0 | 0 | 100% | 100% | The "CodeFlow-only" edges are imports that work because a test changes `sys.path` at runtime (flask's conftest prepends `tests/test_apps`; a django test inserts its own directory) — real, and invisible to any static truth. CI runs the click check. --- ## Real vs heuristic vs experimental Not everything here is the same kind of thing, and the difference matters more than the feature list. | Capability | Kind | What that means | |---|---|---| | Import graph | **Real, measured** | Relative imports, `.js`→`.ts` (NodeNext), tsconfig/jsconfig `paths` + `baseUrl` (with `extends`/`references`), workspace packages, Python relative + absolute (src layout) imports, Go modules (`replace`, `go.work`, nested modules, GOPATH-era repos), Java (imports, same-package types, on-demand and static imports, any source layout), C/C++ (`#include` in the compiler's search order; calls reach the defining file). Scored against tsc, `go list`, javac and clang above. Committed JS bundles (webpack/browserify/Parcel) are left out rather than reported as hundreds of broken imports. | | Call graph, centrality, blast radius | **Real** | Computed from parsed source. Deterministic: same commit in, byte-identical numbers out. Key-file ranking counts production imports only, so heavily-tested files do not outrank load-bearing ones. | | Import cycles | **Real** | **Load-time** cycles only: `import type`, `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, imports inside function bodies and dynamic `import()` cannot cause an import-order failure and are excluded — on Zod, tRPC and Flask that is the difference between dozens of reported cycles and the true number, zero. | | Citation check of arbitrary text | **Real** | Does the file exist, are the cited lines inside it (physical line count), is the named symbol declared there? It proves a reference points at something real — not that the prose around it describes that code correctly. | | PR impact (`impact`, GitHub Action) | **Real** | Dependents, entry points, tests that reach the change, new load-time cycles and imports that resolve to nothing — from the import graph of both sides of the diff. | | Symbol extraction (JS/TS/JSX/TSX/Python/Go) | **Real** | tree-sitter WASM. JS/TS/Python measured against authored ground truth in `packages/eval`. | | Community detection (Louvain) | **Real** | Seeded and canonically relabelled, so two runs of the same graph give the same partition. | | Citation grounding | **Real** | Structural — see above. Enforced at the point of production, and shared as one predicate between the app, the eval and the verifier harness. | | Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector → RRF → rerank → MMR) | **Real** | The refusal floor is compared against the vector arm's raw cosine, before fusion, so "I don't know" stays meaningful. | | File-role classification, entry-point detection | **Heuristic** | Pattern-based (paths, manifests, and a declared `main` in the code). Usually right, occasionally not, and never presented as more than a classification. | | "Test files that reach it" | **Heuristic** | Import reachability, **not** coverage. Labelled that way in the UI because there is no coverage data. | | AI summary, reading order, inferred domains | **Model output** | Grounded and labelled as inference wherever shown. The parser's structural roles sit on a different tab for exactly this reason. | | Specialist fan-out over communities, best-of-N | **Experimental** | Flag-gated (`FANOUT_SYNTHESIS`), off by default, and **unproven at real scale** — there is no measurement against a live model showing it produces better output than the single-shot stage. | | Model routing, parallel stages | **Experimental** | Flag-gated, off by default. The measured speedups are orchestration-only, on a hermetic harness with mock providers. | | Speculative prefetch | **Experimental, opt-in** (`SPECULATIVE_PREFETCH=true`) | Builds the RAG chunk plan while synthesis waits on the provider. The overlap is proven on the hermetic harness; it stays off until a run against a real provider shows it pays for its CPU. | --- ## Honest limits - **Language coverage is narrower than "any codebase".** Deep support — symbols, call edges and a measured import graph — covers **JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX, Python, Go, Java, C# and C/C++**. Rust and PHP are next; until then they get line counts only, so `find_references`, callers and blast radius return little of use on those repositories. The pipeline degrades gracefully; it does not pretend. - **The AI stages need your key.** No key means no summary and no Q&A. The map, the metrics, the cycles and the communities all still work. - **The fan-out is opt-in.** It is 5N+1 provider calls where the single-shot stage is 1. With it off, the Domains tab is hidden rather than empty. - **Local-CLI search is lexical only.** The offline embedder is feature hashing, not a transformer: it finds chunks that share *words*, not meaning. See [Analyse a private repo](#analyse-a-private-repo-offline). - **Cost reports tokens always and dollars only if you price them.** `usd` is `null` until `LLM_PRICING` is set, with the unpriced models named. Tokens are read from the provider's own counters either way. - **The graph does not see imports inside `declare module` blocks**, or `import`/`require` calls built from non-literal strings. Both are rare; the accuracy table above counts them. - **`impact` needs the base commit locally.** It runs local git only (`diff`, `merge-base`, `archive`) and never fetches, so CI checkouts need `fetch-depth: 0`. - **Nothing is deployed, and the AI stages have not run against a live provider.** The graph numbers above are measured on real repositories; every AI-side number comes from a hermetic suite with mocked providers. `DESIGN.md` §6 lists what still needs a real service. --- ## Architecture A pnpm + TypeScript monorepo. Four services over three data stores. ``` ┌───────────┐ enqueue ┌──────────┐ → MongoDB (results, caches) Browser → │ web (SPA)│ ─────────────────→ │ api │ → Redis (queue, budget, limits) │ :5173 │ ←── SSE progress ── │ :4000 │ → Postgres (pgvector — the Q&A index) └───────────┘ └────┬─────┘ │ job ┌────▼─────┐ git clone + Gemini / Anthropic / Voyage │ worker │ runs the 8-stage pipeline └──────────┘ ``` | Path | What it is | |------|-----------| | `apps/web` | React 18 + Vite SPA. No UI framework, no chart library. | | `apps/api` | Express + SSE. Can also host the worker in-process (`RUN_WORKER_IN_PROCESS`). | | `apps/worker` | BullMQ consumer — clones, parses, calls the providers. | | `apps/mcp` | MCP stdio server exposing the graph + retrieval + a verifier to a coding agent. | | `apps/local-cli` | `codeflow-local` — offline analysis, no key, no network. | | `packages/*` | `analyzers` (pipeline), `agents`, `graph`, `parsers`, `retrieval`, `memory`, `observability`, `arena`, `eval`, `shared-types`, `config` | The dependency map in the UI is a **radial layout rendered as hand-written inline SVG — no graph library**. Distance from the centre is fan-in rank, so the most depended-upon modules sit in the middle. It replaced a force-directed graph deliberately: force layouts are non-deterministic, so two loads of the same repository produced two different pictures and neither said which module was load-bearing. See `DESIGN.md` for the reasoning behind this and the other significant choices. --- ## Run it locally (Docker) The whole stack — web, API, worker, MongoDB, Redis and Postgres — runs with **one command**. You need Docker and your own free Gemini API key. ### Prerequisites - **[Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)** installed and **running**. - A **Gemini API key** (free) — get one at **https://aistudio.google.com/apikey**. CodeFlow never ships a key; you use your own, and it stays on your machine. ### 1. Get the code ```bash git clone https://github.com/AnshulMohanty/Code_Flow.git cd Code_Flow ``` ### 2. Add your API key Create a file named **`codeflow.env`** in the project root with a single line: ``` GEMINI_API_KEY=your-key-here ``` > `codeflow.env` is git-ignored — your key is never committed. ### 3. Start it ```bash # macOS / Linux ./start.sh # Windows start.bat # …or run the command directly (any OS) docker compose --env-file codeflow.env -f docker-compose.app.yml up -d --build ``` The **first run builds the images (a few minutes)**; later starts are quick. ### 4. Open the app Go to **http://localhost:5173** and paste a public GitHub repo URL, for example: ``` https://github.com/jamiebuilds/the-super-tiny-compiler ``` ### Ports | Service | URL / Port | |---------|------------| | Web UI | http://localhost:5173 | | API | http://localhost:4000 | | MongoDB | 27017 | | Redis | 6379 | | Postgres (pgvector) | 5432 | Postgres is **required for Q&A across processes**: the worker writes the index and the API reads it. Without it both fall back to a private in-memory index and every question comes back "I could not find that" — `GET /health` reports which one you actually have, under `retrieval`. ### Manage it ```bash docker compose --env-file codeflow.env -f docker-compose.app.yml logs -f # follow logs docker compose --env-file codeflow.env -f docker-compose.app.yml down # stop docker compose --env-file codeflow.env -f docker-compose.app.yml down -v # stop + wipe the local databases ``` --- ## Analyse a private repo, offline No key, no network, no code leaving the machine: ```bash npx codeflow-local analyze . # graph, metrics, cycles, communities + a lexical index npx codeflow-local ask . "where are retries handled?" ``` Parsing is tree-sitter WASM, the embedder is in-process, and the index is a file on disk. No provider client is ever constructed on this path, and the published bundle contains no `fetch` call and no provider hostname — `apps/local-cli/src/__tests__/zeroEgress.test.ts` checks both, and you can grep the file you installed. It stops at a complete deterministic analysis plus a searchable index. **There is no AI summary**: synthesis needs a model and there is no keyless local one, so rather than degrade into something that looks like a summary and is not, it says what it cannot do. Search is lexical — shared identifiers and path words, not meaning. **Speed.** Each file's parse is cached under its content hash in `.codeflow/cache` (add `.codeflow/` to your `.gitignore`), so a re-run parses only what changed; `--no-cache` turns it off. Measured on Kubernetes (26,558 files) on an Apple M5 laptop, Node 26: | Run | Wall time | Peak memory | |---|---:|---:| | Full analysis, no cache | 20.7 s | 1.07 GB | | First run, filling the cache | 25.6 s | 1.01 GB | | Re-run, nothing changed | 7.7 s | 0.74 GB | | Re-run after editing one file (2 files parsed) | 7.8 s | — | The graph is identical across all four — checked edge for edge. `impact` analyses the head and the base of a PR in one process and parses every untouched file once. **Under load** (the Docker stack, `scripts/load-test.sh`): 26 public repositories covering every supported language are submitted at once, each from its own client IP as PR bots would, while 20 simulated users poll job status, open results and hit `/health`. Every job is a real clone and analysis (a fresh cache namespace per run). Measured on 2026-11-16 on the same laptop, Docker Desktop: | Workers | Jobs done | All jobs finished in | Throughput | Job end-to-end p50 / p95 | API p95 (reads) | Slowest request | Errors | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 26/26 | 58.5 s | 26.7 jobs/min | 25.7 s / 56.9 s | ≤ 50 ms | 76 ms | 0 / 8,487 | | 2 | 26/26 | 29.7 s | 52.5 jobs/min | 14.8 s / 26.9 s | ≤ 33 ms | 115 ms | 0 / 4,529 | | 4 | 26/26 | 17.1 s | 91.1 jobs/min | 7.6 s / 14.8 s | ≤ 42 ms | 103 ms | 0 / 2,533 | Throughput scales 1.97x at 2 workers and 3.4x at 4 (the 4-worker run is short enough that the slowest repositories set its end). A worker running its default two jobs peaked at 499 MiB. --- ## Claude Code alone vs Claude Code + CodeFlow Give an agent the CodeFlow MCP server and it can ask the resolved graph instead of searching file by file. `scripts/agent-bench.mjs` measures whether that helps: headless Claude Code (Sonnet), the same question and the same read-only tools (Read, Grep, Glob) in both arms, the second arm also connected to CodeFlow over MCP. The answer to every question is a set of files, and the **truth comes from the compiler** (javac / clang, the same truth as the accuracy tables above), so CodeFlow never grades itself. Measured on 2026-11-16, 76 runs in all: | Question | Repository | Arm | Precision | Recall | Median time | Median turns | Cost (4 questions) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **Impact** — "if F changes, what is affected, directly or indirectly?" (14–38 files) | jsoup (Java) | Claude alone | 1.00 | 1.00 | 19 s | 6 | $0.227 | | | | **+ CodeFlow** | 1.00 | 1.00 | **12 s** | **3** | **$0.139** | | | libuv (C) | Claude alone | 0.78 | 0.99 | 22 s | 6 | $0.400 | | | | **+ CodeFlow** | 0.79 | 1.00 | **18 s** | **3** | **$0.217** | | **Direct** — "which files depend on / does F depend on?" (3–6 files) | jsoup, libuv | both | 0.97–1.00 | 1.00 | ~10 s | 2–3 | equal | On impact questions the agent with CodeFlow answered in half the turns at **40–46% lower cost**, with the same accuracy: one `get_blast_radius` call instead of a chain of searches. On direct questions it is a tie — one grep for a class or header name is already the whole answer, and that is reported here rather than left out. Read it as a pilot: 4 questions per kind per repository, one run each, mid-size repositories (about 215 and 380 source files); larger repositories, where a search returns far more, are next. Two fixes came out of the runs themselves: MCP server instructions that route question phrasing to a tool (the agent had used CodeFlow in 2 of 4 runs; now 8 of 8), and full lists for MCP clients (a 25-item cap, sized for the internal agent, sent the client searching for the rest). The libuv precision of ~0.79 is the same in both arms and comes from the truth, not the agents: clang's truth is one Linux build, and both arms rightly name files that reach `uv/tree.h` only through Windows-only headers. --- ## Check an answer or a PR Three model-free checks, all offline: ```bash # 1. Every code reference in a piece of text — an AI answer, a PR description, a review comment. # Exit code 1 when any reference is wrong. pbpaste | npx codeflow-local verify . - # ✓ packages/analyzers/src/stages/rag.ts:128 `createRagStage` — declared at line 125-369 # ✗ apps/worker/src/index.ts:9999 — line 9999 is outside the file (412 lines) # ✗ packages/config/src/loader.ts — no file "packages/config/src/loader.ts" in this repository # 2. What a change set touches, against its merge-base with main. npx codeflow-local impact . --base main # text npx codeflow-local impact . --base main --format markdown # a PR comment npx codeflow-local impact . --base main --fail-on new-cycle,broken-import ``` **Run only the tests a change can affect.** `codeflow-local tests . --base main` prints the test files whose import closure reaches a changed file (plus changed tests, and Go package tests). A change the graph cannot trace — `package.json`, a lockfile, a config, CI — selects every test and says why. Proven by fault injection (`scripts/test-selection-eval.mjs`): break a source file so it throws on load, run the **whole** suite through the real runner, and check every failing test was selected. On CodeFlow's own suites, measured 2026-11-16: | Suite | Faults injected | Failing test files observed | Missed | Test files skipped (mean) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | `packages/analyzers` (25 test files) | 20 | 91 | **0** | 80% | | `packages/parsers` (14 test files) | 12 | 102 | **0** | 39% | **Keep architecture boundaries.** A committed `codeflow.rules.json` (`"from": "apps/web/**", "forbid": "apps/worker/**"`) is checked on the resolved graph by `codeflow-local check` and, for a PR's changed files, by `impact --fail-on rule` — so an import through a workspace package name or alias is caught, which a text search for the path misses. This repository's own layering is a rules file, enforced in CI. **Find files nothing uses.** `codeflow-local unused` lists source files that nothing imports, includes or calls — conservatively (JS/TS, Python, C/C++ headers; entry points, convention files and scripts a `package.json` runs are excluded). A list to review, not to delete blindly. **3. On every pull request** — and **quiet by default**: it comments only for a new cycle, a broken import, a rule violation, an untested change to a file 5+ files depend on, or a wrong reference in the PR description, and updates its earlier comment once those are fixed. Replayed over real history (`scripts/replay-history.mjs`: the same `impact` the action runs, on each of the last 50 commits of zod, jsoup and Hugo — 150 commits, all of which passed those projects' own CI), it would have stayed silent on all 150: no false alarms. What it catches is shown by the fault-injection runs above and the fixture tests; healthy history simply has nothing to catch. ```yaml # .github/workflows/codeflow.yml on: pull_request permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write } jobs: impact: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: { fetch-depth: 0 } - uses: AnshulMohanty/Code_Flow@main with: fail-on: new-cycle,broken-import,rule,wrong-citation # optional # quiet: "false" # comment on every push instead ``` **For coding agents**, the MCP server's `verify` scope adds `verify_citations` (check a draft answer before showing it) next to `verify_answer` (grade a structured claim such as "who calls X"). > `codeflow-local` is not on npm yet — `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes it on a `v*` tag. Until > then, run it from a checkout: `pnpm --filter "codeflow-local..." build && node apps/local-cli/dist/index.js `. > The GitHub Action builds it from source in the job. --- ## Configuration All runtime config is environment variables — [`.env.example`](.env.example) has the full list with what breaks without each one. For the Docker run above, the only thing you must provide is `GEMINI_API_KEY`. | Variable | Default | Notes | |----------|---------|-------| | `GEMINI_API_KEY` | — | **Required** for stages 7–8. One key powers both chat and embeddings. | | `LLM_PROVIDER` | inferred | `gemini`, `anthropic` or `openai`. More than one key set with no explicit choice throws at boot rather than guessing. | | `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` | inferred | `gemini`, `voyage` or `openai`. Gemini recommended — Voyage's free tier allows 3 req/min. | | `MONGO_URI` / `REDIS_URL` / `POSTGRES_URL` | local containers | Point at managed services for a cloud deploy. | | `CORS_ORIGINS` | — | Comma-separated browser origins. Until it is set the browser gets CORS errors against a healthy API. | | `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` | `0` | Reverse proxies in front of the API (Render: `1`). Without it every visitor shares the proxy's IP, so the per-IP rate limit becomes one global bucket. | | `RUN_WORKER_IN_PROCESS` | `false` | Runs the worker inside the API — one service instead of two, for a free tier. | | `MAX_REPO_FILES` / `MAX_REPO_BYTES` | `25000` / 512 MB | Largest clone the worker accepts. Size it to memory: an analysis needs about 150 MiB + 30 KiB per file (measured: Kubernetes, 26,595 files, 890 MiB), times `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`. | | `LLM_PRICING` | — | JSON model→price. Unset ⇒ `usd: null` with the models named. | | `FANOUT_SYNTHESIS` | `false` | The experimental specialist fan-out. Also the only thing that fills the Domains tab. | --- ## Local development Run the apps from source with hot reload, using Docker only for the data stores. ```bash pnpm install --frozen-lockfile # Node 20 + pnpm 9 docker compose up -d # mongo + redis + pgvector (dev stores only) cp .env.example .env # then set GEMINI_API_KEY pnpm dev:api pnpm dev:worker pnpm dev:web ``` Quality gates — **hermetic**: no network, no keys, no service containers, and zero skipped tests. ```bash pnpm -r typecheck # type-check all 16 workspaces pnpm test # serial vitest suite pnpm -r build node --test tests/*.mjs # root suite ``` **1534 vitest tests (99 files, 15 packages) + 26 root tests**, all passing — measured on the commit that introduced this line, not estimated. CI runs the same four commands plus parser-parity, a keyless eval check, the graph-accuracy gate against tsc, and a Docker smoke test that builds the three images, boots the stack and runs a real analysis through it (`scripts/docker-smoke.sh`). > Note (Windows): run installs one at a time — concurrent `pnpm install`s corrupt the > node_modules link step. --- ## Troubleshooting - **First `docker compose up` is slow** — it builds three images from source; later starts reuse the cache. - **"Could not reach the API"** — check the `api` container is healthy and `CORS_ORIGINS` matches the web origin (`http://localhost:5173` by default). - **Every question answers "I could not find that"** — `curl localhost:4000/health | jq .retrieval`. If `mode` is `memory`, Postgres is not reachable and the API is querying an index the worker never wrote to. - **Run says "partial" / no Q&A index** — an embedding call was rate-limited. Keep `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=gemini`; Voyage's free tier allows only 3 requests/min. - **A port is already in use** — change the host port under `ports:` in `docker-compose.app.yml`. --- ## Docs | File | What it is for | |------|---------------| | `DESIGN.md` | How it is built and why, the critical decisions, the process (develop, verify, deploy, operate), and the roadmap with current status. |
